decisions.reason: Fouling detection automation is part of the firm's announced digital, energy-efficient infrastructure direction and likely stems from funded R&D, so management keeps it and attributes slow uptake to long municipal procurement cycles.

As the hardware counterpart to Product A that the firm has publicly showcased, the fouling detection system carries visible commitment and sunk development costs, so management persists despite only modest website presence.
The spring-controlled flap weir sits close to the core hydraulic steelwork business, needs little extra investment to maintain, and is too young for weak results to be read as anything but temporary.
The energy management system is central to the firm's stated push toward networked, efficient water infrastructure with energy recovery, so management strongly commits to it.
The overflow flap gate line has several models and its own website page, reflecting substantial investment and visible commitment in a core product area, so withdrawal is very unlikely.
